title: Derived pullback along an isomorphism of schemes is the termwise inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$, with coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_Y$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] equal to the constant sheaf $(A_{E,n})_Y$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and to the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and similarly on $X$. Let $c_\Lambda:g^{-1}\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ be the structure isomorphism of the inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]: for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ it is $c^g_{A_{E,n}}$; for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ it is the composite $g^{-1}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_mg^{-1}(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\varprojlim_mc^g_{A_{E,m}}}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_X$. Then for every complex $K$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules whose class lies in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the termwise inverse image $g^{-1}K$, made a complex of $\Lambda_X$-modules through $c_\Lambda$, has its class in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, and there is an isomorphism
$$
 \lambda_K:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g^{-1}K
$$
in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, natural in $K$, where $Lg^*$ is the derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. In particular, for $K=\Lambda_Y$ placed in degree $0$, $\lambda_{\Lambda_Y}:Lg^*\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}\Lambda_Y$.

proof.text: Construct the commutative finite-quotient tower and the cone with vertex the recorded completed coefficient ring. Forgetting commutativity identifies it with the defining limiting ring-sheaf cone, so reflection of limits proves it limiting. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] inverse image preserves this limit; its natural invertible constant comparisons identify the pulled-back tower with the target tower. Uniqueness of limit objects gives the completed ring isomorphism, its projection equations and its uniqueness. For modules, the underlying abelian comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-inverse-image-comparison] identifies the forgetful composite with exact abelian inverse image. The faithful exact forgetful functor reflects finite limits, finite colimits and additivity. This proves exactness of the recorded module inverse image with action transported along the inverse coefficient isomorphism.

proof.text: For finite coefficients, apply [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] to the canonical constant-ring comparison. Its naturality gives a natural isomorphism from the ringed module pullback to termwise inverse image with transported action. The direct-image structure map is the transpose of that same coefficient comparison. Hence the ringed pullback and the recorded intrinsic pullback are left adjoints to naturally isomorphic right adjoints; uniqueness of left adjoints identifies them. Apply exact-functor derived localization to these natural isomorphisms. This compares the recorded finiteDerivedPullback with isomorphismFiniteTermwiseInverseImage on the entire ambient derived category, with no resolution choices.

proof.text: Convert constructibility of a constant-ring module sheaf to constructibility of its module-valued sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility]. Descend a constructible pro-etale sheaf to the etale site, apply the established pullback-stability theorem [prop-constructible-pullback], and use the comparison between etale pullback and pro-etale pullback. Transport back through the module encoding. Exactness identifies homology of the termwise pullback with pullback of homology, so it preserves the finite cohomological support and constructibility of every cohomology sheaf. Transfer this property along the two ambient natural isomorphisms from step 2. Fullness lifts their composite to the constructible subcategories; evaluate the ambient comparison at the finite coefficient object for the last clause.

source.place: Coefficient objects and constructible coefficient categories; direct application of their definitions under the site relabelling

proof.text: Compare sectionwise inverse image with the recorded inverse image over the completed rings. The site map/pullback adjunction induces the sectionwise sheaf adjunction. Transporting scalars along an invertible ring map gives the analogous module adjunction: its triangle identities follow from the sheaf triangles and cancellation of the ring map with its inverse. On constant sheaves, sheafification uniqueness and naturality of constant sections identify the transposed sectionwise coefficient map with the canonical direct-image map. Compose completed maps with every finite quotient projection; the defining limit-lift equations and naturality of both adjunction units reduce equality to this constant case. The direct-image module functors are therefore naturally isomorphic. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies sectionwise module inverse image with ringed tensor pullback, and [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] identifies the latter with the recorded transported-action functor. Exact derived localization gives an ambient natural isomorphism of their derived functors.

Obtain a coherent reduction/total-limit calculus S from [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization] supplies isomorphisms from completed pullback to sectionwise inverse image of S-completion, natural in every ambient derived morphism. Its stalk-unit assumptions follow from invertibility in the residue fields by the local-ring unit criterion. On the intrinsic constructible category, [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] supplies invertibility of the actual reconstruction unit for its calculus T. T and S have the identical right adjoint, the specified total limit. Uniqueness of left adjoints and its unit compatibility formula transfer invertibility to the unit of S. Assemble its components into a natural isomorphism on the constructible full subcategory. Compose the normalization isomorphism, inverse image of the inverse reconstruction unit, and the ambient comparison of step 4 to obtain the required natural comparison with transported-action inverse image.

[lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] puts completed pullback of every intrinsic constructible object in the target intrinsic constructible category. Transfer that property across the natural comparison using isomorphism closure from [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Fullness lifts the comparison to the constructible categories. For the integral coefficient specialization, choose a prime different from l, the field ZMod p and its algebraic closure to instantiate the auxiliary finite-field datum of [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. That theorem applies to any scheme without a structure morphism to this finite field and supplies both membership and derived completeness of the regular coefficient object. Evaluate the constructed natural comparison at this object. The finite specialization already follows by evaluation of the ambient isomorphism in step 3.
